text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card and the language is cautious, with usable next steps and example claims. But the narrative has several internal contradictions and misreadings that would make an investigator redo analysis, notably the claim that excess is mostly on multi-morbid patients while also saying the share is above the all-provider share in every stratum, plus a misleading 0-of-19 sentence and an unsupported 'rule check' reference.","problems":["The 0 of 19 sentence is phrased confusingly (\"had no lab or test line\") and reads as if no notes lacked labs; the card says of_those_no_lab_on_claim is 0, which is ambiguous. The later \"no sign of data-reviewed inflation\" is a stronger conclusion than warranted.","The headline says most of the excess falls on multi-morbid patients, yet the rationale says the 99215 share exceeds the all-provider share in every stratum. Several strata (0 conditions: 0 of 9) do not, so the claim is inaccurate. The statement that complexity does not explain the excess 'the risk-adjusted score already accounts for' is muddled.","Says 'rule check places it between cutoffs', which has no support in the evidence card.","Claims 'most supported notes have no time recorded' and asks to check for templated text, but the 4 supported example claims are mostly generic; C0071743 is cited neither as high-complexity nor tied to the documentation point.","The example claims in the summary list cite only 2 of 3 low-complexity claims and omit any high-complexity claim in the formal citations, though C0071602 and C0071657 are mentioned in the text and not in cited_claim_ids.","Next steps are generic: they ask for a larger sample of 99214 and 99215 claims and a re-screen, without naming specific claims to request, though the rationale does name them.","The 22% vs 11% comparison rests on 2 of 9 charts; the summary acknowledges this but still says documentation 'leans mildly against' billing."]}
